response.sql:
WITH item_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    oi.order_item_id,
    COUNT(ili.invoice_number) AS ili_count,
    AVG(CASE 
      WHEN ili.derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL AND ili.derived_total_cost != 0 
      THEN ili.product_price / ili.derived_total_cost 
      ELSE NULL 
    END) AS avg_ratio
  FROM Order_Items oi
  LEFT JOIN Invoice_Line_Items ili ON oi.order_item_id = ili.order_item_id
  GROUP BY oi.order_item_id
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_average_ratios,
  AVG(ili_count) AS avg_of_line_item_counts
FROM item_stats;

assumptions.assumption: "Skipping missing ratios" means excluding rows where `derived_total_cost` is NULL or 0 (preventing division by zero), not merely skipping NULL results from missing data

alternatives.interpretation: "Missing ratios" refers strictly to NULL values in operands (either `product_price` or `derived_total_cost` is NULL), with the assumption that `derived_total_cost` is never 0 in the data
